books.title: The Fracture
books.note: Uses a different authoring format than loop/scale (no MOVEMENTS/CH JS literals found) — not yet extracted. Do not invent chapter data.

movements.name: The machine that has no motive
movements.blurb: Why this is different in kind from every other manipulation in this library — and why there is no villain to confront.

chapters.title: You are reading this on it
chapters.blurb: No other book in this library is in this position. The reflex to check something else mid-chapter is the subject arriving in person.

chapters.title: Nobody designed this
chapters.blurb: The most important idea in the book. The manipulative configuration was not authored. It was found, by a search that had no opinion.

chapters.title: The asymmetry
chapters.blurb: A skilled human manipulator gets a few dozen observations a day. This gets billions, forgets nothing, and never has a bad week.

chapters.title: What it optimises for
chapters.blurb: Engagement is a proxy. The metric and your wellbeing agree for a while, then separate — and the system keeps climbing.

chapters.title: The eight stages, ported
chapters.blurb: The Fractal’s architecture applied to a feed. The match is not metaphorical, and this chapter says why.

movements.name: The mechanics
movements.blurb: The specific machinery, named. Everything here was tested against millions of people and kept because it won.

chapters.title: Variable reward
chapters.blurb: Fixed rewards produce satisfaction. Unpredictable ones produce checking. Your feed’s inconsistency is the feature.

chapters.title: The removal of stopping cues
chapters.blurb: Every older medium ended. Endings are where people decide whether to continue, and they were engineered out.

chapters.title: The interrupt
chapters.blurb: A claim on your attention you never granted per instance — and a recovery cost that appears in no usage statistic.

chapters.title: Dark patterns: the interface as adversary
chapters.blurb: Not sloppiness. Measured, tested, and kept because the honest version scored worse.

chapters.title: Manufactured obligation
chapters.blurb: Streaks, badges, progress bars. Manufacturing a debt where none existed. This library deploys none of them, and says why.

chapters.title: The numbers
chapters.blurb: What happens to social response when it acquires a public integer — and to a person when their worth does.

chapters.title: Outrage as fuel
chapters.blurb: You are not seeing what people believe. You are seeing what spreads. Mistaking one for the other is the era’s defining error.

chapters.title: Ranking is an argument
chapters.blurb: Every ordered list makes a claim while presenting as neutral. You cannot see what you were not shown.

movements.name: The economy
movements.blurb: Who pays, who is paid, and what is actually being sold. Follow the money and the design decisions stop being mysterious.

chapters.title: You are not the customer
chapters.blurb: And not quite the product either. What is sold is predicted and influenced future behaviour, which is worse.

chapters.title: The auction in two hundred milliseconds
chapters.blurb: What happens between the tap and the page: a profile of you is offered, bidders bid, someone wins the right to reach you.

chapters.title: What it knows, and what it infers
chapters.blurb: Almost nothing you typed. Enormous amounts derived — including things you have told no one.

chapters.title: The consent that isn’t
chapters.blurb: Agreement obtained by exhaustion is a coercion pattern everywhere else in this library. Legality does not change what it is.

chapters.title: The desperation premium
chapters.blurb: Different prices for different people, set by inferred urgency. The person who can least afford it reliably pays most.

chapters.title: Where the money actually goes
chapters.blurb: The sibling of The Fracture. Who captures the value, and how little reaches whoever made the thing.

movements.name: The machine in other rooms
movements.blurb: This is not a social-media problem. The same machinery schedules your shifts, prices your groceries, and ranks your dates.

chapters.title: Algorithmic management
chapters.blurb: Coercive control with an API — shift fragmentation, routing that prices a bathroom break, dismissal by system.

chapters.title: The gambling convergence
chapters.blurb: Loot boxes, gacha, currencies that hide real cost. Gambling mechanics migrated into products sold to children.

chapters.title: Optimised against your success
chapters.blurb: A service whose revenue depends on continuation, selling an outcome that ends continuation. No conspiracy required.

chapters.title: The manufactured want
chapters.blurb: The shortening path from seeing to owning, and how to tell a want you had from one that was made for you.

chapters.title: Politics, honestly
chapters.blurb: The most contested territory here. What targeting can and cannot demonstrably do, with the strongest case on both sides.

movements.name: What it does to belief
movements.blurb: Manufactured agreement, the pipeline, the collapse of evidence — and an honest account of where the research is contested.

chapters.title: Manufactured consensus
chapters.blurb: How the appearance of agreement is produced, and why volume is not evidence of prevalence.

chapters.title: The bubble, honestly
chapters.blurb: The research is genuinely mixed. This chapter presents it fairly, then makes the narrower claim it can support.

chapters.title: The pipeline
chapters.blurb: How gradients move people toward extremity one reasonable step at a time. The mechanics, not any one ideology.

chapters.title: Nothing is true
chapters.blurb: The subtler damage is not believing false things. It is losing the capacity to believe anything.

chapters.title: Synthetic evidence
chapters.blurb: The photograph has stopped being proof — and the second-order problem is worse than any single fake.

movements.name: What it does to you
movements.blurb: Comparison at industrial scale, the performed self, the loss of unwatched life, and machines built to be exactly what you want.

chapters.title: Engineered inadequacy
chapters.blurb: Comparison at industrial scale, where the inadequacy and the remedy are sold by the same system.

chapters.title: The performed self
chapters.blurb: What happens to identity when it is continuously published, and to changing your mind when the record is permanent.

chapters.title: The loss of unobserved life
chapters.blurb: The quietest chapter. Unwatched space is where people experiment, fail, and become someone.

chapters.title: Attention debt
chapters.blurb: Separating the myth from the measurable finding — and why the real one makes recovery possible.

chapters.title: Parasocial capture
chapters.blurb: One-sided intimacy with people who do not know you exist. Real feeling, absent relationship.

chapters.title: Synthetic intimacy
chapters.blurb: Always available, never bored, never critical, continuously optimised to be what you want. The frontier, in both directions.

chapters.title: Preference, created
chapters.blurb: It does not merely measure what you like. It changes it, then measures the changed version, then optimises further.

movements.name: The counter
movements.blurb: What actually works, starting from the admission that you cannot out-willpower an optimiser.

chapters.title: What good design looks like
chapters.blurb: The reference sample. You cannot identify manipulative design without a baseline for the other kind.

chapters.title: Why \u201cjust delete it\u201d fails
chapters.blurb: Structural reasons, not personal ones — including the class dimension nobody wants to name.

chapters.title: Changing the optimisation target
chapters.blurb: You cannot out-willpower an optimiser. You can frequently change what it is optimising against.

chapters.title: Friction, deliberately
chapters.blurb: Reintroducing the endings that were engineered out. Environment design, not discipline.

chapters.title: Withdrawal, honestly
chapters.blurb: What the first fortnight actually feels like, described plainly so nobody is blindsided into shame.

chapters.title: Rebuilding attention and appetite
chapters.blurb: Attention as a trainable capacity — and the less-discussed half, the recovery of appetite for slow things.

chapters.title: Using it on purpose
chapters.blurb: The anti-Luddite chapter. The problem was never the technology. It was the target behind it.

movements.name: The ledger
movements.blurb: What this book might have wrong, how to help someone else, and what has to happen at a scale larger than you.

chapters.title: The algorithm as scapegoat
chapters.blurb: A framework that explains everything explains nothing. The Weighing, applied to this book’s own material.

chapters.title: What this book might be wrong about
chapters.blurb: The history of technology panics, fairly told — and the specific findings that would falsify this book.

chapters.title: Helping someone else
chapters.blurb: For the reader worried about a teenager or a parent. Confrontation and confiscation reliably fail.

chapters.title: What actually works, and what is coming
chapters.blurb: At collective scale. Built by no villain, unfixable by willpower — which means the response has to be structural.

movements.name: Why weigh at all
movements.blurb: The problem this book solves, the safeguard against its own misuse, and the three frames everything downstream rests on.

chapters.title: You learned to see. This is how you learn to weigh.
chapters.blurb: Detection asks whether something resembles a tactic. Weighing asks whether that is the best explanation for what happened.

chapters.title: This book in the wrong hands
chapters.blurb: Every argument in these pages is also what an abuser says. Three rules, before anything else.

chapters.title: The two errors, and what they actually cost
chapters.blurb: Missing real manipulation and inventing it are both real failures. Their costs invert depending on where you are.

chapters.title: Most people, most days
chapters.blurb: Base rates, in plain language — and the honest exception for anyone currently inside an unusual room.

chapters.title: The gradient
chapters.blurb: Rude, thoughtless, unkind, harmful, controlling, abusive. Collapsing these is the most common calibration failure there is.

movements.name: The instrument is you
movements.blurb: Before evidence: the detector itself. Where yours was calibrated, what distorts it, and what a healthy baseline actually looks like.

chapters.title: Your detector has a history
chapters.blurb: Your pattern-recognition was tuned by a specific room. It is still tuned to that room.

chapters.title: The gut: sensor or smoke alarm
chapters.blurb: The most-cited evidence people offer, taken seriously — and then sorted.

chapters.title: Grief in the costume of analysis
chapters.blurb: Building a case is easier than feeling a loss, and it works. That is the problem.

chapters.title: The retrospective rewrite
chapters.blurb: After a revelation, every memory changes at once. Some of that is accurate. A total overwrite is not.

chapters.title: The state you’re judging from
chapters.blurb: Judgment is a physical act performed by a body. No verdicts at 2am.

chapters.title: The reference sample
chapters.blurb: You cannot calibrate without a baseline. What ordinary, decent, non-manipulative relationships actually look like.

movements.name: What counts
movements.blurb: Evidence standards. What is a pattern, how a case builds itself, and the two riskiest sources of information you will ever use.

chapters.title: What is evidence
chapters.blurb: What was said and done, versus what it felt like and what you inferred. Both matter. They are not the same tier.

chapters.title: One thing is not a pattern
chapters.blurb: Frequency, duration, escalation, and response to feedback — the four dimensions that turn incidents into findings.

chapters.title: The file that builds itself
chapters.blurb: Once someone is under suspicion, everything they do becomes evidence. Including kindness.

chapters.title: The discipline of three explanations
chapters.blurb: The book’s central working exercise, and the one you will use most days.

chapters.title: The boring explanations
chapters.blurb: Incompetence, exhaustion, fear, bad skills. Manipulation is a high-effort explanation. Do not reach for it first.

chapters.title: Intent, impact, and the mind-reading trap
chapters.blurb: What they did, what it did to you, and what they meant are three questions. Only two are knowable.

chapters.title: Secondhand accounts
chapters.blurb: Most judgments are made on information someone else supplied. The highest-risk evidence category there is.

chapters.title: Judging strangers through screens
chapters.blurb: Clips, screenshots, threads — an adversarially curated sample, and the verdicts we build from it.

movements.name: The tests that work
movements.blurb: Four discriminators that actually separate manipulation from ordinary human failure — and the safety gate that comes before all of them.

chapters.title: Before you test: is testing safe?
chapters.blurb: Several tests in this movement introduce friction on purpose. With a dangerous person that is the worst advice in this book.

chapters.title: The naming test
chapters.blurb: Describe the behavior plainly and watch what happens. The strongest single discriminator here.

chapters.title: Repair, and apology’s counterfeit
chapters.blurb: Everyone causes harm. What happens afterward is the whole signal.

chapters.title: The cost of \u201cno\u201d
chapters.blurb: Refuse something small and reasonable. Watch the price. Track the pattern, not the reaction.

chapters.title: Is it you, or is it everyone?
chapters.blurb: Behavior aimed only at you, only unobserved, means something different from behavior aimed at the world.

chapters.title: Power changes the meaning
chapters.blurb: The same words from a peer and from someone who controls your housing are not the same words.

chapters.title: Difference is not malice
chapters.blurb: Culture, neurotype, class, generation, language. A large share of false positives live here.

chapters.title: Institutions weigh differently
chapters.blurb: No single mind to read, so intent is the wrong question. Incentive and structure are the right ones.

movements.name: The mirror
movements.blurb: Turning the instrument around before you act on anything it told you.

chapters.title: Am I the one doing it?
chapters.blurb: Everyone uses these tactics sometimes. Someone who has learned the vocabulary can use them with precision.

chapters.title: The vocabulary as a weapon
chapters.blurb: Clinical language confers power. It can end a legitimate grievance as easily as it can name one.

chapters.title: Who benefits from your verdict
chapters.blurb: Nobody weighs alone. Everyone helping you has a stake, including the people who love you.

chapters.title: Being wrong well
chapters.blurb: Calibration is meaningless if you cannot reverse. The repair you owe, and how to make it without a second grievance.

movements.name: Living calibrated
movements.blurb: What to do with a conclusion, how to survive not having one, and how to get back to trusting people.

chapters.title: Assessment is not decision
chapters.blurb: You do not have to prove harm to be entitled to act. These are two different questions.

chapters.title: When you can’t ever know
chapters.blurb: Some questions never resolve. How to close a loop without a verdict.

chapters.title: Scoring your own past calls
chapters.blurb: The only mechanism here that keeps improving after you finish the book.

chapters.title: Certainty is the tell
chapters.blurb: People who just escaped one total explanation are the prime recruiting pool for the next.

chapters.title: Helping someone else weigh
chapters.blurb: You will be handed other people’s situations. The friend who escalates fastest is rarely the friend who helps most.

chapters.title: When weighing stops
chapters.blurb: The floor, at full strength. Children, violence, isolation, impossibility of leaving, physical fear.

chapters.title: Trust as a skill you rebuild
chapters.blurb: If I can never be certain, how do I get close to anyone again? The question the whole book exists to answer.
